programme.title: Chernobyl: Inside the Meltdown
programme.desc: On April 26, 1986, an explosion destroyed the fourth block of the Chernobyl power plant.The accident was caused by design defects in the reactor and errors during the safety test.It was the worst nuclear disaster in history.The explosion released 400 times more radiation than the bomb dropped on Hiroshima.40 years after the tragedy, its consequences will be shown - from KGB activities to military operations in Ukraine.There will be plenty of witness accounts that will shed new light on the dramatic events.The speakers will include:liquidator working on the roof of reactor 3 and journalist Wyatt Andrews, who was covering the information blockade in Moscow On April 28, the remains of the fourth reactor were still unextinguished.The authorities finally decide to evacuate.50,000 people take supplies for three days.They don't know that they will never return to their homes.Meanwhile, firefighters with burns are being watched by the KGB.Swedish technicians at the Forsmark nuclear power plant are the first to detect increased levels of radiation.They alert the world about the catastrophe that the USSR authorities are trying to hide.Events two weeks after the explosion will be discussed.The authors will explain how attempts were made to hide the truth.
